answer: An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the harbor index resolves every citation against the cedar checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the atlas audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 259 aliases therefore pays the authoring cost 259 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature.
